verdicts.reason: Both use the same three-column banner, and both shrink the jar's SOLSTICE label until it can't be read. Both also break SHOP SOLSTICE onto two lines so it competes with the headline. A pushes the jar closer to the left edge (about 60px) and sits a little unevenly. B's jar has slightly more inset, so its margins are more even.

These are practically the same: centered logo on top, jar on the left, Glow. in the middle, and a two-line CTA on the right. Both share the same flaws: the jar label is too small to read, the CTA wraps and nearly matches the headline in weight, and the jar floats with dead space around it. B's jar and headline are only slightly larger.

A keeps the sun-and-SOLSTICE logo centered at the top, as in the original. B moves the logo to the bottom under Glow., shrinks it so small the wordmark is barely legible, and places it off the headline's axis. In B the brand reads as an afterthought and the reading order is broken.

A drops the logo to a tiny, off-center spot below Glow., where it is unreadable and loses its brand role. A's jar also crowds the left edge. B keeps the logo centered at the top with sensible margins; its only flaws are the shared ones: unreadable jar label and a two-line CTA.
